d9fda1aa96: The greatest common divisor (GCD, also called highest common factor) of two integers is the largest integer that divides both. The least common multiple (LCM) is the smallest positive integer that both divide. They are used to simplify fractions, to add fractions (the LCM of denominators), and to synchronise repeating cycles.
b6f58fc1bb: Prime factorisation: write each number as a product of primes. The GCD takes the smallest exponent of each shared prime; the LCM takes the largest exponent of every prime present.
058b564b85: Euclid’s algorithm: repeatedly replace (a, b) by (b, a mod b) until the remainder is 0; the last non-zero remainder is the GCD. It is far faster for large numbers, because it never needs to factorise.
